content: Endometriosis occurs when the tissue that normally lines the inside of the uterus grows in areas where it should not. Nafarelin is a medication used to treat this condition. Additionally, it is prescribed for children to manage a specific type of early puberty known as central precocious puberty, which is gonadotropin-dependent. Nafarelin functions similarly to a natural hormone produced by the body called gonadotropin-releasing hormone (GnRH). Before using nafarelin, carefully read the Medication Guide and any Patient Information Leaflet provided by your pharmacist. Follow the illustrated instructions for proper use, including performing test sprays into the air if using a new bottle. Gently blow your nose before administering the medication. Typically, this medication is used twice daily, approximately every 12 hours, as directed by your doctor. If more than one spray is required, wait 30 seconds between sprays. Avoid spraying the medication into your eyes and refrain from sneezing during or immediately after use, as this may reduce the amount of medication absorbed. Follow the detailed instructions for cleaning the spray tip. It is crucial to use this medication exactly as prescribed by your doctor and not to skip any doses. Consult your doctor or pharmacist to determine how long each nasal spray bottle should last. Do not use the bottle beyond the recommended duration, even if medication remains, as the full dose may not be delivered. Do not increase the dose or use the medication more frequently or for longer than prescribed. When starting nafarelin, symptoms may temporarily worsen. For women treating endometriosis, this could include increased vaginal bleeding. For children managing early puberty, symptoms such as increased breast size, pubic hair growth, oily skin, or body odor may occur. These symptoms typically improve after the first month of treatment. Common side effects in children may include nasal irritation, hot flashes, or vaginal discharge. In women, side effects may include nasal irritation, hot flashes, headaches, decreased sexual interest, muscle pain, vaginal dryness, acne, or a decrease in breast size. Remember, this medication is prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. Serious allergic reactions to this medication are rare. Before using nafarelin, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it, to GnRH or similar hormones (e.g., leuprolide), or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other issues. Nafarelin must not be used during pregnancy, as it may harm an unborn baby. Women should begin this medication between days 2 and 4 of their menstrual cycle. While periods and ovulation may stop during treatment, this is not a reliable form of birth control. Discuss non-hormonal birth control methods, such as condoms or diaphragms with spermicide, with your doctor. It is unknown if this medication passes into breast milk, so breastfeeding is not recommended while using nafarelin due to potential risks to the infant. Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. Keep a list of all products you use, including prescription and non-prescription drugs and herbal products, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Nafarelin may interfere with certain lab tests, such as those assessing pituitary gonadotropic and gonadal functions, potentially causing false results. In case of overdose, if someone experiences severe symptoms such as passing out or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. Regular lab and medical tests, such as growth and bone age velocity in children, should be conducted while using this medication. Keep all medical and lab appointments. If you miss a dose, use it as soon as you remember. If it is near the time of the next dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. Store the bottle upright at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not freeze or store it in the bathroom. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. This information is a summary and does not include all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this medication and your specific health needs.
